/marketplace/batches/{id}/ — takes a lookup key and returns a single object carrying id and created_at, yet is marked side_effect_risk "none". Listing it per the standing rule, but I judge the author's reasoning sound and did NOT probe a novel id: the client is a plain DRF retrieve (`async batch(t){await e.get(BATCH_BY_ID(t))}`), the key is an autoincrement pk not a natural key, and the model needs filename/channel/uploaded_by/row_count/summary which a pk-only get_or_create could not construct. Corroborating: batch ids stayed 29-51 contiguous across every probe in this session. Residual gap is unchanged — nobody has confirmed it 404s cleanly on an unknown id. Recommend the CLI hard-require that the id came from `batches` output rather than accepting a free-typed integer. Separately, NOT added to this list because they fail the id/created_at criterion, but flagged for the reviewer: /marketplace/warehouse-insights/ and /marketplace/reconciliation/ both accept `channel` — the exact key that triggered the get_or_create on /marketplace/settings/ — and return a single object. They are aggregates with no id/created_at and cannot plausibly create a row, but the spec's mitigation (restrict --channel to the observed enum FLIPKART|AMAZON, verified as the only two values in MpChannelSelect and in useMpChannel's localStorage default) must be enforced on EVERY command in this domain, not just the ones where channel is required.

/marketplace/settings/ — NOT a genuine read/write mix-up (the author's intent is correct and emphatic), but a structural placement hazard that must be fixed before assembly: this path sits INSIDE the `endpoints[]` array — the machine-readable list a generator iterates to emit commands — with command_name "DO-NOT-PUBLISH" and side_effect_risk "confirmed-mutates-on-get". The safety depends entirely on a downstream tool reading a magic string in a name field. It has a real PUT verb and a GET that provably creates production rows. Move it out of endpoints[] into excluded_writes[] (where it already has a line) so nothing can emit it by accident. No other write leak found: all twelve published paths include GET in their harvest methods array, and the three dual-use GET+POST paths (/marketplace/sku-mappings/, /marketplace/combos/, /marketplace/warehouses/) are correctly published GET-only and flagged. The three PATCH+DELETE detail routes were re-verified live as 405 on GET: /marketplace/sku-mappings/111/, /marketplace/combos/3/, /marketplace/warehouses/1/ all return {"detail":"Method \"GET\" not allowed."}.

/wms/{collection}/{id}/ - the only published path whose side-effect risk is asserted rather than tested. Marked side_effect_risk 'none' but never probed (the spec says so itself), and the same URL is GET + PATCH + DELETE. Should be 'unverified'. NOTE: no live probe was added here either - correctly, since testing it needs a keyed lookup.

NO CONFIRMED SIDE EFFECT ANYWHERE IN THE DOMAIN. Positive evidence collected this run: keyed lookups in this domain 404 on a key they do not own rather than creating it (JIVO_MART GET /warehouse/bst/172/ -> 404 while the same id is 200 on JIVO_OIL; GET /wms/cell-purposes/ -> 404). A get_or_create would have returned 200 with a fresh row. /warehouse/bst/sap-transfers/{doc_entry}/ re-confirmed: response carries no id/created_at/updated_at (keys are exactly document_type, doc_entry, doc_num, doc_date, from_warehouse, to_warehouse, warehouses, comments, reference, card_code, card_name, line_count, total_quantity, total_boxes, lines) - a pure SAP projection.
